NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)  
The proposed intervention is to introduce a hydrophobic nano-clay interlayer between the ethylene-vinyl alcohol (EVOH) layer and adjacent polymer layers in the multilayer film structure. Standard practice relies solely on the inherent barrier properties of EVOH, while this mitigation adds a tortuous-path barrier mechanism that physically impedes moisture and oxygen diffusion regardless of EVOH's plasticization state. The closest existing technique is nanocomposite barrier films (e.g., montmorillonite clay in polyolefins), but this differs by embedding the nano-clay as a discrete interlayer rather than dispersing it in the bulk polymer, allowing it to maintain barrier integrity even when EVOH fails.

PHYSICS CHECK  
The governing relation is Fick's first law of diffusion: J = -D·(Δc/Δx), where J is flux, D is diffusivity, and Δc/Δx is concentration gradient. The nano-clay interlayer reduces D by creating a tortuous path, increasing the effective diffusion path length (Δx) by a factor of L/L₀, where L is the actual path and L₀ is the straight-path distance. For a 5 wt% nano-clay loading with aspect ratio 100, the tortuosity factor is ~10, reducing D by ~90%. This maintains WVTR below 0.5 g/m²/day even when EVOH's D increases 10× due to plasticization.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Replace existing adhesive layer between EVOH and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) with a co-extruded interlayer of polyethylene (PE) containing 5 wt% montmorillonite nano-clay (b)  
- Adjust co-extrusion die gap to 100 μm (maintaining total film thickness) (c)  
- Modify lamination temperature to 220°C (within existing equipment range) (c)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
| Standard Practice | Proposed Intervention | Burden Impact |  
|-------------------|----------------------|--------------|  
| PET/EVOH/PE lamination | PET/nano-clay-PE/EVOH/PE | Same (co-extrusion equipment) |  
| Adhesive application | Eliminated | Lower (no adhesive curing) |  
| Total thickness | 100 μm (unchanged) | Same |  
| Operating temp | 220°C | Same |  
Conclusion: Same burden class (no new hardware, same processing steps)

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Accelerated aging test per ASTM F1249 at 40°C/75% RH for 6 weeks (equivalent to 18 months at 25°C/65% RH). Instruments: MOCON OX-TRAN™ WVTR tester, calibrated to ±0.01 g/m²/day. Pass/fail: WVTR ≤0.5 g/m²/day at all intervals. Kill criterion: Any single measurement >0.5 g/m²/day. Duration: 6 weeks. Falsification: Control samples (standard film) will show WVTR >0.5 g/m²/day within 3 weeks; intervention samples maintaining ≤0.5 g/m²/day for 6 weeks confirm effectiveness.
